note:
PASS/FAIL position. This fragment now audits with 0 FAILs and 244 nodes (down from 292), and the whole tree audits at 0 FAILs / 70 WARNs, so nothing here blocks the build. Two WARNs attributable to this file are left deliberately, both of the same shape as ~35 accepted ones elsewhere in the tree: c64.packaging.litho-press is kind "tool" under category "packaging", and c64.packaging.kraft-process is kind "note" under category "packaging". The audit's CAT_OK table does not allow tool or note under packaging, but an offset press is capital equipment and the kraft-versus-bleached node is commentary; retyping either to satisfy the table would make the node less true. The remaining 29 WARNs against this file are the tree-wide r4 duplicate-name rule, which fires on any duplicate group anywhere in the tree; 11 of those groups contain one of my nodes and every one of them is resolved by a merge above.

Contradiction to flag, not mine to fix. 30-passives.json describes the C64 keyboard as 63 keys with double-shot moulded legends (c64.keyboard-switches.*). The service manual and this fragment both say 66 keys with pad-printed legends, and c64.keyboard now states why the 63 figure circulates: it is a count of matrix domes plus the cursor keys rather than of the keys a user presses. RESTORE is off-matrix (dedicated NMI line) and SHIFT LOCK shares the left-shift lines, so 64 matrix positions + RESTORE + SHIFT LOCK = 66. Whoever owns 30-passives should reconcile it; I have not touched that file.

Shared tables. data/_ingredients.json still carries "abs bezel surface": "c64.case.abs-resin", which is the input that used to assert the rainbow badge was made of ABS. Nothing uses it any more - c64.case.logo now takes its inputs from c64.decor.pad-print.ink and c64.decor.metallised.flake, and its note records the correction - but the stale mapping is still in the shared table and should be deleted. The "chem.benzene" and "chem.chlorine" entries in data/_aliases.json look intentional (they redirect legacy ids onto chem.styrene.benzene and the cracker chlor-alkali node), so I left them alone. data/_fixes.json no longer holds any entry for this fragment, so every kind here is now set at source and the fixes table is not load-bearing for 40-chassis.json.

Deliberately not proposed. c64.case.other-polymers.cumene and c64.case.other-polymers.methanol have no canonical material node to fold into (chem.propylene.cumene and chem.pom.formaldehyde are both processes, not substances), so they stay as they are until the petrochemical fragment publishes the materials. c64.case.abs-resin.pgm-ore is PGM from ore while metal.palladium is PGM from anode slime - related but not the same node, and I would rather not guess. c64.case.abs-resin.phthalic-anhydride has no obvious home either. c64.case.abs-resin.san-resin, .additives and .emulsion-polymerisation are marked structural above because they parent most of the other merges in that block; apply the leaves first. Finally, a note on a house-wide pattern I chose not to touch: 151 nodes across the tree (34 of them mine) list one of their own children in `inputs`, so build emits a `from` edge that duplicates the `children` edge. It is noisy but it is consistent across every fragment and no rule flags it, so changing only my file would make my fragment the odd one out.
